chapter: Cotton Club and radio fame with Cab
title: Alternating with Duke, the Duffy payoff and 'Minnie' becomes the theme
summary: Cab and Duke trade the Cotton Club between road tours, the downtown club is arranged by giving Duffy 25 percent, and the band discovers its theme song on the road.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So I don't know how I got around... But, see, Cab got big, and we started going on the road when Duke was in the Cotton Club.
And then they just started alternating, because both bands got big where they could go on the road. So when Duke would go out, we'd go in.
So they finally... How they worked in the thing downtown, they made a deal with Duffy, to give Duffy 25

percent of the Cotton Club. That's the only way. See... I don't know whether you want to call them gangsters or whatever, but the Bosses... They didn't go in nobody's territory unless they got the okay. So they made okay a deal with Duffy for him to get 25 percent, because Duffy was the kingpin in that part of New York. Because we had played in a little club downstairs on 149th Street. That's how we got to know the guy that was the head of the Stork Club... Not the Stork Club; another big club on the East Side.
Oh, I know what you mean.
The big club. Played all the big stars.
Yeah, I know. I can't think of the name now.

I can't think of the name right now. But anyway, we played for him. He even played Calloway over there later. But when we were in the Cotton Club, Stark still was the manager. So then that's when we got... I'll tell you who had a lot to do with the Cotton Club. The writer...
No. But Walter Winchell, man... Any time we did a show, it was a terrific show. But I don't think Walter Winchell ever had a tab. That's just something I

think. But I'll tell you, every time he'd come to the Cotton Club we had to play that damn "Minnie The Moocher." But when we went on the road the next year, we found out we had a hit. We had a theme song. And see, we wasn't too cool about theme songs. We were just getting in the big time. We didn't know what a theme song was. When we went on the road, everybody was asking for "Minnie The Moocher," and then we started enjoying playing it, because this was our trip to glory.
